# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, AI Governance Academy
**Source basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with headquarters in the Netherlands. The Client is at a piloting stage of AI maturity and has three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although the start date is not fixed.

Your stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three stated constraints shape the work:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This proposal treats both as systems the AI Management System (AIMS) should attach to rather than duplicate. The Profile names these frameworks but does not identify the specific registers, procedures or records they contain. For that reason the integration points below are shown as `Unknown` until the build team confirms the attaching artifacts in Week 1.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would hand the Client a finished set of documents. The Guided AI GRC Build takes a different approach. Your own team builds the system each week with structured workshops, coaching and asynchronous work between sessions. When the program ends, the people who will operate the AIMS are the people who wrote it.

This approach suits Tamarack for three reasons:

1. **The inventory finding concerns ownership as much as documentation.** A team that has built and populated the inventory itself is positioned to keep it current.
2. **The visual inspection deadline continues past Week 12.** The Client will need internal capability to apply the governance to production deployment in Q2 2027 without external dependency.
3. **The future ISO/IEC 42001 effort depends on internal competence.** Readiness for that effort rests on whether the Client's people can explain and run their own management system.

The program works from three open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), used for the steering layer

It is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

### Inventory and assessment priority (Weeks 2 to 5)

Systems enter the inventory and assessment work in this order:

1. **Customer service chatbot.** It is deployed, it faces customers and it touches customer data subject to GDPR and the EU residency constraint.
2. **Visual inspection pilot.** It is the system tied to your Q2 2027 objective and the one most likely to touch production staff, which brings in the works council constraint.
3. **Sales forecasting.** It is entered as a planned system so that governance precedes deployment.

The Week 2 inventory will also record any further AI systems the team identifies. It directly addresses the June 2026 internal audit finding.

### ISO/IEC 42001 mapping

The ISO/IEC 42001 column shows the readiness theme each week supports. It describes preparation only. It does not represent a certification, audit or conformity outcome.

### Week-by-week plan

| Week | Focus, tailored to the Client | Key artifact | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point (ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS / ISO 9001 QMS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles; agree steering attendees; record the works council consultation requirement | Draft AIMS charter and role matrix | Context, leadership and roles | `Unknown` |
| 2 | AI system inventory: chatbot, visual inspection pilot, planned forecasting, plus any systems surfaced | Populated inventory | Scope and context | `Unknown` |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a functioning minimum viable AIMS, defined as:

1. Adopted charter.
2. Populated inventory.
3. Operating risk register.
4. Adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

Element 5 needs your attention now. The chatbot is the only use case the Profile records as deployed. The visual inspection system is recorded as a pilot, and the Profile does not state whether that pilot counts as production use. The second governed workflow is therefore `Unknown` at this stage. It will be confirmed as a Week 1 decision, informed by the Week 2 inventory. Any candidate workflow that touches production staff will follow works council consultation (confirm with external counsel).

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All hours below are estimates. They cover the weekly workshop, the coaching session and asynchronous work, and will be refined in Week 1. Steering preparation is additional.

| Role | Typical week (estimate) | Peak weeks | Peak week (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 hours | 1, 3, 6, 12 | 5 hours |
| CISO | 4 hours | 3, 7, 8 | 6 hours |
| Head of Quality | 4 hours | 7, 10, 11 | 6 hours |
| Head of Data | 5 hours | 2, 4, 10 | 7 hours |
| German plant manager | 2 hours | 4, 9, 10 | 5 hours |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 hours | 11, 12 | 5 hours |

We recommend that Week 1 confirm how the two internal auditors participate. An advisory and assurance role helps preserve their independence for later reviews of the AIMS.

## 6. Steering Cadence

The executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** approves scope, team and the second workflow approach.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** receives the attestation against the six-element definition and a 12-month operating plan.

Steering attendees beyond yourself as Sponsor are `Unknown` and will be confirmed at Week 1. The steering layer draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format:** Twelve weeks, each with one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Session times will be set in Week 1. Team locations and time zones are `Unknown`.

**Price:** US$60,000, which falls within the US$80,000 budget approved this fiscal year. Payment terms and contract language carry legal effect (confirm with external counsel).

**Timing:** The start date is `Unknown`. As a scheduling calculation only, a start in the first full week of January 2027 would place Week 12 in late March 2027, before Q2 2027 begins. This leaves the Client a period to apply its governance to the visual inspection production decision. It is not a guarantee of production readiness.

## 8. Next Step

We propose three actions:

1. **Before 15 December 2026:** a 45-minute call to confirm the start date, steering attendees and build team availability.
2. **By your decision date:** your approval to proceed.
3. **On approval:** we issue the Week 1 mobilization brief and the engagement agreement for review (confirm with external counsel).

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
